questions.q: What do I need to register to vote in South Dakota?
questions.a:
You will be asked to provide documentary proof of US citizenship when you register to vote in South Dakota.

Acceptable documents include:

- A South Dakota driver's license or non-driver ID issued after July 1, 2025
- A driver's license or ID from another state that shows citizenship was verified
- A tribal identification card

OR a copy of one of the following:

- Birth certificate
- US passport
- Consular Report of Birth Abroad
- Certificate of naturalization
- Other documents allowed under federal guidelines

If you do not provide proof of citizenship when you register, you may be registered as a federal-only voter, which means you can vote in federal races (like President and Congress), but not in state or local races.

questions.q: How do I register to vote?
questions.a:
South Dakota requires a paper registration form with your original signature.

- Fill out the voter registration form (https://sdsos.gov/elections-voting/voting/assets/FINAL-VoterRegistrationForm_Part1.pdf)
- Sign it
- Submit it to your County Auditor (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

Your form must be received at least 15 days before an election to vote in that election. You cannot submit your registration by fax or email.
